evidence.quote: {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|rank|t=strong, proud}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ranc|t=proud, haughty, arrogant, insolent, forward, overbearing, showy, ostentatious, splendid, bold, valiant, noble, brave, strong, full-grown, mature}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rank}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rankaz|t=straight}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-|t=straight, direct}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|rank|t=slender, slim}}, {{cog|nds|rank|t=slender, projecting, lank}}, {{cog|da|rank|t=straight, erect, slender}}, {{cog|sv|rank|t=slender, shaky, wonky}}, {{cog|is|rakkur|t=straight, slender, bold, valiant}}. The sense referring to taste or odor is possibly influenced by {{m|en|rancor}}.

"row, line, or series;" c. 1400, a row of an army, from Old French renc, ranc "row, line"… See origin and meaning of rank. from Old French renc , ranc "row, line" (Modern French rang ), from Frankish *hring or some other Germanic source (compare Old High German hring "circle, ring"), from Proto-Germanic *hringaz "circle, ring, something curved" (from nasalized form of PIE root *sker- (2) "to turn, bend").
